📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, if we're using Metacritic as a metric, Grand Theft Auto 6 is currently the best-reviewed game of all time. Between preorders and launch-day sales, it's already made over $3.7 billion in sales revenue. It's being lauded as a landmark achievement in game design, storytelling, and engineering. So how, exactly, did Rockstar pull it off?

Well, the billion-dollar production budget certainly helped. But a Bloomberg report offers an vital insight into how GTA 6 was able to deliver on its promises: According to a spokesperson, 21% of Rockstar's staff—roughly 1,000 people—have been employed by the company for over 10 years. For many of its development leads and directors, that figure is closer to 20 years, or higher.

Industry observers note that by retaining its employees for so long, Rockstar is able to capitalize on the kind of shared, institutional knowledge and honed creative process that developers build through years of collaboration. We've seen that same kind of continuity at other studios who've delivered some of the last decade's biggest hits: FromSoft director Hidetaka Miyazaki has attributed its wins with Elden Ring and Armored Core 6 to its developers growing with the studio, while the breakout sales successes of Baldur's Gate 3 and Helldivers 2 were delivered by developers who'd spent years sharpening their craft at Larian and Arrowhead.

That lesson—that making successful games is easier when you keep the people who know how to make games around—isn't one that the games industry at large has been adhering to: In its latest game developer survey, GDC reported that 34% of its respondents had been laid off in the last two years. 20% of laid-off respondents said they'd been laid off twice or more in 24 months.

In a recent development, from Halo to Dragon Age, we've seen how beloved game franchises can suffer when their studios endure employment turmoil. After it laid off 1,600 Xbox workers in July, Microsoft's own employees mentioned that myopic job cuts at major game companies were weakening the games industry as a whole by dismantling its ability to produce quality games.

It's a bell we've been ringing a lot around here.

In a recent development, still, while Rockstar boasts a deep roster of veteran employees, those devs aren't confident that they won't be the next ones suffering from mass layoffs: We've seen plenty of successful introduces lead to job cuts in recent years. As the organization enjoys GTA 6's record-breaking launch, fears like those are why over 1,600 Rockstar employees in the UK are presently voting on unionization.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the very popular and critically-acclaimed The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has set another record.
  • In a recent development, the remake has sold more than 1m physical copies in the US alone in its launch week (ending 7th November).
  • According to recent reports, while Nintendo games tend to perform better at retail than those from Sony, Xbox or third-party publishers, physical sales in general have been declining in the US.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the very popular and critically-acclaimed The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has set another record. After selling 5.2m copies in four days and becoming the Switch 2's fastest-selling game, Ocarina of Time has now been revealed to also be a major seller at retail.

In a recent development, the remake has sold more than 1m physical copies in the US alone in its launch week (ending 7th November). That's according to Circana analyst Mat Piscatella, who revealed on Bluesky that the record also makes it the first title to surpass 1m physical sales since 2023's Tears of the Kingdom. That is, no other game - from any publisher - has managed to sell over 1m copies in the US within its first week in three years.

According to recent reports, while Nintendo games tend to perform better at retail than those from Sony, Xbox or third-party publishers, physical sales in general have been declining in the US. In July, Piscatella revealed that just seven PlayStation games have sold more than 100,000 physical copies up to that point in 2026, and that was after all the backlash to Sony's decision to end physical disc manufacturing by January 2028.

Recent findings suggest that ocarina of Time's lead of this particular segment likely won't continue, however. That's because, as Piscatella pointed out in a follow-up post, Circana's tracking considers disc-less, code-in-box versions to be physical editions. This means Grand Theft Auto 6 will likely overtake the remake in short order, just as it's expected to break records elsewhere.

In Eurogamer's glowing review of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, Christian Donlan argued that Nintendo has done just enough to modernise a timeless classic while maintaining what made the original so special for many players.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Home Alone is one of the most beloved Christmas movies ever.
  • Recent findings suggest that it hurts my heart, and it hurts my heart that every Christmas I have to deal with this.
  • Roebuck has had a busy career since, including major roles in movies like The Fugitive and Agent Cody Banks, but he never worked with Columbus again.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home Alone is one of the most beloved Christmas movies ever. Families watch and rewatch it every year around the holidays. For most, it’s a celebratory time, but for one actor, Daniel Roebuck, it’s bittersweet. Roebuck, if you didn’t know (and I didn’t), was the original actor cast in the role of one of the Wet Bandits, Marv, who was memorably played by Daniel Stern. Behind the scenes of Home Alone, Roebuck was fired by director Chris Columbus just four days into filming, and ever since, Christmas has meant he has to relive that tough moment.

In an interview with PageSix, Roebuck explained:.

Recent findings suggest that it hurts my heart, and it hurts my heart that every Christmas I have to deal with this. I have the utmost respect for Chris Columbus. When he did fire me, and he said he’d put me in his next movie, I waited by the phone, man.

Roebuck has had a busy career since, including major roles in movies like The Fugitive and Agent Cody Banks, but he never worked with Columbus again.

Recent findings suggest that this all stemmed from a story Columbus recently recounted about filming Home Alone on The Wildmen Podcast, where the director explained that the studio would only pay for either Daniel Stern or Joe Pesci (who played Marv’s partner Harry), but not both. So Roebuck was cast and, according to Columbus, the first screen test with Roebuck and Pesci was “terrible.” Roebuck, however, disputes that version of the story, telling PageSix:.

They never, ever, ever filmed me and Joe Pesci together. I never, ever filmed anything with Joe Pesci. The camera never rolled on us.

He added that he only worked with Pesci for one day. He also adds that, despite Columbus telling him they would work together (something Columbus also notes), that never happened, and they haven’t spoken since. Roebuck still doesn’t understand the reasoning behind his firing, but he doesn’t have any ill will towards Columbus, saying:.

I can’t speak to his motivations. He’s a good Catholic guy. I try to be a good Catholic guy. I try to be a man of faith, and I’m certainly a man of forgiveness. So I never held a grudge against him for firing me. I’m disappointed that every Christmas I have to put up with this when I’ve contributed so much more to the world than not being in ‘Home Alone.'.

It has been revealed that ultimately, though, Roebuck didn’t star in the movie, and, at least according to Columbus, the director got the actor he wanted all along. It’s pretty hard to imagine the movie without Stern, but these events bring a little bit of a dark cloud over the casting. I guess in the end, Columbus did what he thought he had to do, but it’s easy to understand why Roebuck has mixed feelings about what many consider one of the best Christmas movies ever.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A judge has denied a motion to dismiss a US lawsuit against chip makers Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron.
  • In a recent development, the class action suit was filed at the United States District Court for the Northern District of California in June this year.
  • Recent findings suggest that the trio of companies deny having colluded, arguing in a new motion to have the case dismissed (thanks, IGN) that this suit simply retreads old ground covered in a previous antitrust case and quoting deceased judge Richard Posner.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A judge has denied a motion to dismiss a US lawsuit against chip makers Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron. The suit acccuses the companies of fixing RAM prices and supply, thereby contributing to worsening the effects of the ongoing memory crisis.

In a recent development, the class action suit was filed at the United States District Court for the Northern District of California in June this year. It accuses Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron of moving in lockstep away from production of consumer-focused DDR3 and DDR4 RAM and towards HBM memory more typically used in AI datacenters. The suit claims that "in a competitive commodity market", "at least one of three large producers, seeing record prices, would expand output of the product whose price was rising", thereby forcing their competitors to either follow suit or risk losing out on customers.

Recent findings suggest that the trio of companies deny having colluded, arguing in a new motion to have the case dismissed (thanks, IGN) that this suit simply retreads old ground covered in a previous antitrust case and quoting deceased judge Richard Posner. "[C]ompetitors in concentrated markets watch each other like hawks," was the Posner quote they wheeled out, which I mention because otherwise the response I'm about to lay out will sound like a very weird tangent.

"But Plaintiffs’ allegations go beyond hawks watching each other," judge Noël Wise wrote in her order to deny the dismissal motion. "Their contentions are more akin to hawks flying in formation – an activity that hawks ordinarily do not do.".

You know a case is getting serious when facts about Avian behaviour start being wheeled out in response to similes. Bird chatter aside, all this decision means is that the case will rumble on, with both sides still having a chance to present more evidence or make points in their favour before any eventual decision is made by the courts.

So, shelve any hopes you might have of a rapid solution to the memory crisis, which right now looks likely to last until at least 2028.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sci-fi role-playing game Exodus continues to play into the Mass Effect comparisons by revealing the female version of its main character Jun, and with studio Archetype referring to her in marketing material as FemJun.

Recent findings suggest that if that moniker sounds familiar it's because it is: the female Commander Shepard character in the Mass Effect series was nicknamed FemShep. FemShep became an iconic part of BioWare's iconic series, eventually proving that female leads could front games just as successfully as male leads could, and be every bit as popular.

Is the nickname FemJun too blatant? Possibly. But there's well publicised BioWare pedigree at Archetype Entertainment, in the studio's co-founders and in the people leading the project. Key Mass Effect writer Drew Karpyshyn is in charge of writing Exodus, for example, and the similarities to Mass Effect are something the Exodus team has not been shy about in the past. In the wake of Mass Effect 5 being cancelled and BioWare being closed, they become even more alluring.

Industry observers note that there are, however, significant and important differences between Exodus and Mass Effect, key among them, time dilation. In Exodus, there are special Exodus missions whereby you leave your home planet and fly far away, and in doing so experience time differently to the people back home. Many years will pass for them while only days will pass for you, which provides the game with a way to show you long-term consequences of your actions when you return.

It has been revealed that archetype hasn't shown the female version of Jun before, despite having released many videos of Exodus, perhaps to build anticipation for her reveal. It's a press beat that's also provided Archetype - a studio owned by Dungeons & Dragons company Wizards of the Coast - with an occasion to reveal the two actors playing Jun in the game.

Recent findings suggest that female Jun is portrayed by Carina Conti, who played the lead in the recent Mafia game, The Old Country - Isabella Torrisi. She's appeared in HBO's Winning Time and Hulu/Freeform's Good Trouble as well. Male Jun, meanwhile, is portrayed by Stephen Oyoung, who played Mister Negative in Insomniac's Marvel's Spider-Man 1 and 2 games, and Red Hood in Gotham Knights. He also appeared in Mission: Impossible - The Final Reckoning, The Wrecking Crew, and Twisters. The game also famously stars Matthew McConaughey.

Archetype announced a Dark Horse hardback art book to go on sale alongside the game next year as well. This arrives a week after the game; Exodus arrives 7th April 2027 on PC, PS5 and Xbox Series S/X, and the art book on 13th April.

Matt played Exodus at Gamescom relatively recently and came away impressed, referring to it as "the best kind of surprise". "I wasn't expecting quite such a bombastic 45 minutes when I first picked up a controller and settled into Exodus, admittedly, but the more I played, the more it made sense," he wrote. "I might not be much of a Mass Effect fan (damn you M35 Mako once more), but Exodus is now firmly on my radar ahead of its arrival next year.".

If you’re playing GTA 6 and finding it too dark, there’s a good chance you may have your HDR calibration wrong – and no, it’s not your fault!

An extensive research video by HDTV Test – performed on a pricey Sony reference monitor – reveals the game’s HDR calibration may not be working quite as intended.

So while you may have followed the steps perfectly, setting your values until the Rockstar logo is only just visible as instructed, it may not be displaying optimally in your game.

I’d recommend you watch HDTV Test’s video for the full scientific analysis, but in short he explains that the various values in the HDR calibration settings output unexpectedly in-game.

Furthermore, the Rockstar release completely ignores Sony’s global PS5 HDR settings, so while you may have those calibrated perfectly for your particular screen, that won’t help you here.

Here’s how to fix it on PS5, according to HDTV Test – although do keep in mind your optimal personal settings will depend on your display, room, and preferred ambient lighting.

Load the game and press Options > Settings > Display > HDR Calibration.

HDTV Test recommends ignoring Rockstar’s own brightness calibration, so don’t worry too much if the tech giant’s iconic logo is visible or not.

Instead focus on the two sample images of the party on the boat, which you can toggle between light and dark using R1.

These are the recommended starting settings for a display capable of 1,000 nits or higher:.

Feel free to tune these to taste; your own optimal HDR calibration settings will depend on your environment and screen, after all.

But this should help with the overall appearance of the game, and ensure you’re able to see a little bit better in the dark.

Tech Report: Star Wars Galactic Racer will get local split-screen multiplayer in early 2027 with new 'Free Play' mode, finally letting racers yell at one another in a tangible space

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Split-screen multiplayer is often treated by developers as a forgotten vestige of a bygone age, something to be left behind as the standardisation of online play makes it redundant, especially following the pandemic.
  • Recent findings suggest that this newly introduced mode, Free Play, not only allows for local multiplayer of up to four players (with either humans or CPUs racing together), but also for complete freedom of choice in vehicle, character and planet to race on.
  • Recent findings suggest that as for why this feature may not have been available at launch, other than the cynical view that it wasn't considered a moneymaking priority for Fuse Games and Secret Mode, CD Projekt Red senior technical producer Shayna Moon weighed in to theorise that it took some effort to get four separately-rendered views of the game running without making their machine explode like the Death Star.

Split-screen multiplayer is often treated by developers as a forgotten vestige of a bygone age, something to be left behind as the standardisation of online play makes it redundant, especially following the pandemic. It's considered unlikely that you'll have another human being in your home to pick up a controller with you, and since you've inevitably got an internet connection, why not just use that to connect to anyone in the world? I find there's a unique beauty in playing something shoulder to shoulder on a couch with another person, and it seems Fuse Games sees that light too, with Star Wars: Galactic Racer set to be updated to add local splitscreen multiplayer sometime early next year.

Recent findings suggest that this newly introduced mode, Free Play, not only allows for local multiplayer of up to four players (with either humans or CPUs racing together), but also for complete freedom of choice in vehicle, character and planet to race on. A simple versus mode like this is a far cry from the roguelite structure of the main game, and one that draws it closer to its arcade racing game roots. An embracing of that is always welcome, as Galactic Racer has been a reminder to many of just how wonderful the arcade racing genre can be, and how poorly served its been in the industry for a while. For example, while the Fuse Games team is partly made up of Criterion Games veterans, Criterion itself has recently been folded into being a Battlefield Studio by EA, making the future of Need for Speed and Burnout uncertain.

Recent findings suggest that as for why this feature may not have been available at launch, other than the cynical view that it wasn't considered a moneymaking priority for Fuse Games and Secret Mode, CD Projekt Red senior technical producer Shayna Moon weighed in to theorise that it took some effort to get four separately-rendered views of the game running without making their machine explode like the Death Star. As Moon puts it: "To be overly simple about it, if the game is running at 30fps for each player, that means it’s actually rendering 120fps." Likely not an concern for a lot of PC players, but a potential issue for console players considering the game is built to run at a locked 60fps for one player on consoles. Past this upcoming patch, it looks like the Star Wars franchise as a whole could be set for more smaller games ala Galactic Racer in general, per comments made by Lucasfilms' vice president.

Latest Update: PlayStation defeats £2 billion UK lawsuit that alleged Sony forced consumers into "excessive and unfair prices"

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (485 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sony has defeated a major £2 billion UK class action lawsuit concerning the price of games on the PlayStation Store (thanks, TheGameBusiness).
  • In a recent development, the case, brought by Alex Neill, who said she represented roughly 12.2 million gamers, accused Sony of applying "excessive and unfair" pricing on games that appeared on the storefront accessible by PS3, PS4 and PS5 consoles - the PlayStation Store.
  • "Potential PlayStation console purchasers had both access to sufficient information and an incentive to consider that information in order to make informed purchasing decisions at the console level, especially in the case of high-value customers who spend significant amounts in the digital gaming aftermarket," read the judgment.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sony has defeated a major £2 billion UK class action lawsuit concerning the price of games on the PlayStation Store (thanks, TheGameBusiness). The judgment came after a 30-day Competition Appeal Tribunal that took place in London, where PlayStation people claimed Sony had removed "all actual and potential competition" in relation to selling digital games on the console.

In a recent development, the case, brought by Alex Neill, who said she represented roughly 12.2 million gamers, accused Sony of applying "excessive and unfair" pricing on games that appeared on the storefront accessible by PS3, PS4 and PS5 consoles - the PlayStation Store. In a judgment published by the London’s Competition Appeal Tribunal today (17th November), the case was rejected. The judgement noted that market definitions used to define Sony's conduct were "unsafe", and that consumers "would be likely to make informed choices when purchasing consoles" and games on the hardware, too.

"Potential PlayStation console purchasers had both access to sufficient information and an incentive to consider that information in order to make informed purchasing decisions at the console level, especially in the case of high-value customers who spend significant amounts in the digital gaming aftermarket," read the judgment.

It has been revealed that the lawsuit made the argument that, upon purchasing a PS5 or other PlayStation console, you were then trapped within its ecosystem, and forced into paying the prices determined by Sony. The Tribunal disagreed, however, and ruled that Sony competed within a wider 'systems market' alongside Xbox, Nintendo and PC, for example. Furthermore, the Tribunal found no evidence that the existence of other digital storefronts would have actually brought any PlayStation Store pricing down.

Interestingly, the Tribunal used the argument that consumers can also opt and buy physical games instead of using the PlayStation Store - something that is changing as of the start of 2028. That did not seem to have any bearing on today's decision, though. It's also worth noting that this case did not seek to interrogate the ownership status of digital games - something that's been at the heart of the movement rallying against Sony's decision to kill off physical media. Earlier this year, spokespeople from Sony's legal team argued "reasonable consumers" already know they don't actually own their digital games.

It has been revealed that the London Tribunal has a fairly long history. Back in 2022, it began as a case that attempted to sue Sony to the tune of £5bn for "ripping people off" on PlayStation Store. Sony argued the case brought against it in this trial was "flawed from start to finish". This isn't the only situation where we're seeing consumers pursue legal action against the platform holder. Last year, PlayStation was sued in the Netherlands over the so-called "Sony tax" that highlighted artificially inflated prices on the Store, and sought to represent more than 20,000 participants that felt short-changed by the company.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you want to move faster in Grand Theft Auto 6, I can't blame you: There's a lot I've enjoyed about the opening hours I've spent in Jason's shoes. He's handy with a nailgun. He's a good sport when I make him wear the dumbest graphic tees I can find. For a gunslinging drug runner, he's a gentle soul. I just have one complaint.

The man's got a leisurely gait. Which is fine! But there are plenty of times while roaming Leonida when you might wish he and Lucia were moving just a bit faster—just not so fast that you want to force them into a run. Luckily, Rockstar's got our back: There's a setting to bump up your basic movement speed without pushing a button.

It has been revealed that to change the pace that Jason and Lucia move at in GTA 6, head to Settings, move over to the Gameplay tab, and scroll down to the Movement section. The setting you're looking for is Movement Speed.

Sources indicate that this doesn't affect your top speed while sprinting and burning stamina. What it adjusts is the speed you move at when you fully push the joystick. There are four options, each one offering more speed than the last: Walk (the default), Fast Walk, Jog, and Run.

Sources indicate that it's a nice bit of granularity. I go with Fast Walk to give just a slight bump in my base speed without feeling like I'm rushing, but Jog or Run are good options if you really want to cover ground. Whichever one you choose, you can still voluntarily move at a slower pace by only slightly tilting the joystick.

In a recent development, there's also a Combat Movement Speed setting, which—as you might expect—changes the pace you walk at in a gunfight. There are only three options here: Fast Walk, Jog, and Run, because nobody wants to move slowly when they're actively being shot at.

In a recent development, while you're in the menus, I'd recommend digging around to inspect all the available options. Rockstar included a lot of toggles and tweaks for fine-tuning how GTA 6 handles. You can even turn off vehicle damage altogether, if you don't want to pay for car repairs. Not that I've ever crashed or anything. Don't ask my mechanic.

Break up and re-commodify a fallen Earth in Steel Gullet, a satisfyingly funereal factory puzzler that really loves thermodynamics

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It's amazing what a difference a few lines of preamble can make to your understanding of a game.
  • In a recent development, the difference is that you're doing this inside a huge walking fortress city, which stamps across the surface of a largely unseen, devastated and uninhabitable Earth.
  • Recent findings suggest that from a certain, carefully limited point of view, this transforms Steel Gullet into the kind of "Zen experience" I hope death-positive morticians have when really absorbed in their work.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's amazing what a difference a few lines of preamble can make to your understanding of a game. Out now on PC, Steel Gullet is a factory engineering puzzler that, while notable for its meticulous interest in thermodynamics, broadly compares to the foundational work of Zachtronics, together with more recent and focussed conveyor belt wranglers such as Modulus. Resources come in, and you arrange machines on a grid to transform them into something else, before sliding them into an output hopper.

In a recent development, the difference is that you're doing this inside a huge walking fortress city, which stamps across the surface of a largely unseen, devastated and uninhabitable Earth. Your resources are the refuse of a bygone human civilisation: knots of concrete and rebar, flaccid rubber hose and splintered plank, that must be separated out before you can manufacture anything.

Recent findings suggest that from a certain, carefully limited point of view, this transforms Steel Gullet into the kind of "Zen experience" I hope death-positive morticians have when really absorbed in their work. My task is to lay a civilisation to rest, by dissecting and cleansing the remains, readying a fallen objectworld for an after-life that extends somewhere beyond the map's huge rusty walls (walls that, perhaps appropriately, constrain your camera movement a bit too much for comfort).

It makes me think of the vertigo I get when I look at devices such as, well, the computer I'm writing this on, and think about how many materials and histories of production lie entangled within it. Steel Gullet answers the desire for clarity and accounting there. Of course, the other part of the premise is that I am doing busywork for some kind of totalitarian organisation, G.R.I.D. But shh, no time to think about that! I'm trying to work out how hot rubber needs to be before it can be moulded.

Thermodynamics is Steel Gullet's fixation, and a worthwhile one. Every material encased in each lump of salvage has different physical properties – a melting point, density, solubility, ferromagnetism, etcetera. You meed to exploit these differences to separate the pieces. Wood, for example, is more buoyant than metal and concrete, so if you feed the clump into an oil bath, the planks will float to the top. If there's rubber, you can run the clump through furnaces to melt and drain it, then cool and reheat the resulting puddle to create a malleable material.

According to recent reports, it's still just the usual automation game routine of funnelling greebly wotsits through various smashy boxes to produce a commodity. But the thermodynamics sim element both supports the above feeling of purifying a hopelessly muddled world, and makes for a surprising visual feast: I enjoy watching each material emerge from the inital jumble and assume different shapes. There are the usual supporting infrastructure elements, such as elevators, splitters and manual junction boxes. I dare say somebody will build a logic circuit in Steel Gullet, sooner or later - let's start the clock till they get Doom running on the thing.

In terms of overall strategy, you alternate between sending outputs to hoppers that earn you cash, and sending them to hoppers that generate research progression. You'll also unlock newly introduced rooms, removing walls and exposing new output hoppers. As you're issued new work orders, you must break open your production lines to install new machines and redirect the flow. Fortunately, you can sell back components to keep your cash reserves healthy – or at least, you can in the demo.

Recent findings suggest that between chapters, you'll be invited to join the resistance against the aforesaid G.R.I.D., perhaps sending information to the rebels. But again, no time, no time! I have all this concrete I need to powderise, all these girders I need to liquefy and make upcoming, all these crisp, gleaming circuitboards I need to manufacture. The city's hunger is as vast as it is holy. Read more on Steam.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manni L. Perez has been confirmed as the actress behind Grand Theft Auto 6's Lucia Caminos, just days before the game introduces.

As spotted by IGN, the confirmation came during The Game Awards' nominations livestream today, where Perez was nominated for Best Performance for her role as co-lead Lucia.

Perez had been widely rumoured to play Lucia for months, and fans have regularly filled her social media livestreams with questions about GTA 6, which she has been oh-so-carefully sidestepping.

Lucia is one half of GTA 6's lead pair alongside Jason Duval, making it the first Grand Theft Auto game with a playable couple.

Jason's actor wasn't among the nominees, so who plays him is still a mystery.

Perez has previously had guest roles in a string of US TV dramas, including Law & Order: Special Victims Unit, Chicago P.D., The Blacklist, and Blindspot, and has also done voice work for GTA Online.

Funnily enough, Lucia isn't her first Lucia - she also played Lucia Santiago in a 2023 episode of CBS's East Latest York.

In a recent development, GTA 6 arrives 19th November on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. It is now available to pre-load for anyone who pre-ordered the digital version, and those with the code-in-box physical version.

It's long been revealed that GTA 6 will have a regional release, meaning that some lucky, soon-to-be players will be able to access the game much earlier than others. Rockstar's regional release schedule sees the game launching at midnight on 19th November regardless of what region you're in, and if you wish to join those playing almost a day early, there's the good ol' Xbox Newly introduced Zealand trick for eager players to try.

With the PS5 release of Cyberpunk 2077, the Polish studio established itself as an open world significant boy, having previously released one of the greatest RPGs ever in The Witcher 3.

And so it’s only fitting for co-CEO Michal Nowakowski to pour praise on Rockstar’s latest release, now the highest rated game of all time.

“Rockstar Games created a masterpiece that I am planning to explore in the coming weeks and months. Massive congratulations to the whole team who worked on the game. It is unbelievably hard to achieve what you just did. Hats off to all of you.”.

I personally believe it’s going to take years, if not decades, to surpass GTA 6.

The sheer density of the open world, from its dizzying array of art assets to the complexity of its sandbox simulation, is just in another universe to everything else.

Even if you’re not enjoying the game, it’s hard to argue against the standards being set here.

Recent findings suggest that of course, a high bar will raise the levels of absolutely everyone. I personally can’t wait to see what CDPR delivers with The Witcher 4 and its next Cyberpunk game.

10 Indicates Like 'The Traitors' You Should Watch Next

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1329 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that what started as De Verraders way back in 2021 has become a global reality phenomenon: Peacock in the U.S.
  • A reality show with a complex history as relates to The Traitors, the premise being so similar that it may well have served as an inspiration.
  • If there were a prize for dramatic title (and set design), you could do a lot worse than this one.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that what started as De Verraders way back in 2021 has become a global reality phenomenon: Peacock in the U.S. hosts the American version with the sartorially supreme Alan Cumming, and also the earlier UK take as well as iterations from Australia, Canada, and Upcoming Zealand—but there are spin-offs in France, India, Germany, Ireland, Turkey, and more. Basically, throw a dart at a map and you're likely to hit a country with its own take on The Traitors. And yet! The addictive nature of reality TV means that we can't really ever get enough. In that spirit, here's more backbiting reality TV, and a couple of dramas that offer up similarly duplicitous thrills.

A reality show with a complex history as relates to The Traitors, the premise being so similar that it may well have served as an inspiration. Here, players participate in collaborative missions in order to build a prize fund. But it's not all fun and games: There's a secret double agent among the group (the mole, obviously) whose sole task is to undermine the ability of the rest of the group to earn money. Eliminations are done via quiz: The group is grilled on the information they've collected about the mole, and whoever knows the least gets the boot. Originally airing in the aughts, Netflix brought it back for a couple of seasons more recently, with the potential for more to come. Stream the most recent seasons of The Mole on Netflix.

If there were a prize for dramatic title (and set design), you could do a lot worse than this one. In this South Korean reality show, 12 celebrity contestants are challenged to build a prize pot through strategy games. Sometimes they're collaborative, sometimes entirely competitive, and sometimes a blend, but prizes come in the form of "Pieces" that can be won or lost (and that eventually combine to create their own final puzzle). Anyone who finds themselves without a single Piece is out. Pieces can be spent to buy advantages, and also traded, so the show turns on players forming alliances in order to build the prize pot and survive as long as possible. Stream The Devil's Strategy on Netflix.

Here, a bunch of strangers are holed up in an apartment building, cut off from the outside world—and each other. Players can only interact via a custom app, and, thus, can portray themselves however they want, whether that means being 100% genuine (unlikely!) or creating a whole fresh persona. Players judge the competition based on their interactions, determining the "Influencers" who will get to decide on the eliminations. The show ran for seven seasons on Netflix, and is moving to Hulu for the forthcoming eighth. Stream The Circle on Hulu.

You show up at a fancy hotel, and someone hands you a suitcase containing one million dollars. It's yours to keep—as long as you can keep it a secret. In this one, all the contestants get a suitcase, and only one contains the money. Much as with The Traitors, the goal is to figure out who's keeping the secret, with challenges designed to help flush that person out. If the truth is discovered via a vote, that former millionaire is ousted and the money is concealed in another suitcase until the final contestants are given the opportunity to swap bags with someone who they think has the money. Easy come, easy go, I guess. Stream Million Dollar Secret on Netflix.

Recent findings suggest that I'm a little more into the normies on Traitors myself, but there's no question that a big part of the appeal (for most seasons) is watching reality-show celebs go at it with cash on the line. So it is with House of Villains, a Big Brother-style competition with Joel McHale as ringmaster. The core premise is pretty simple: villains (Richard Hatch, Tom Sandoval, Jonny Fairplay, one-time Trump bestie Omarosa Newman, etc.) compete in challenges for rewards and for safety from the inevitable banishment. It's all mostly an excuse to watch some of TV's biggest personalities go for each other's jugulars. Stream House of Villains on Peacock.

Industry observers note that this is not a reality show, but rather a drama about a reality show that may well slake your thirst for treachery while offering up consequences a bit more dramatic than the bruised egos and hurt feelings of The Traitors. Here, eight strangers are selected to compete in a game in which they're locked together in a building and sequestered on different floors each night. They earn money for each minute they last in the game, but all their provisions must be purchased with money they've won, at an extreme markup. At first, the contestants pool their resources so that everyone gets more money—until they learn that people on higher floors are getting more. Then things get nasty Stream The 8 Show on Netflix.

This one plays a bit like The Traitors in reverse: A $250,000 prize pot is, right off the bat, allocated to all 11 contestants who get to hang out in a luxurious villa. So the game isn't about winning money so much as it is about how much you'll keep and how much you're willing to share. Eliminations offer the opportunity to remove those who the others don't want to share with—though contestants don't have to actually ever vote anyone out. They can just keep their portion of the money and hang out, something that obviously does not happen. Challenges along the way force contestants to reveal embarrassing and sometimes ugly truths about themselves that may well put them on the outs with the others. There's only one season at present, though there's potential for more. Stream The Trust on Netflix.

Blending the Major Brother-esque social aspects of Traitors with Survivor's love of the great outdoors, this one drops four teams of four into the Alaskan wilderness (moving to Panama for season three). The contestants are all, by inclination, loners, but the game has only one core rule: Only a team (of at least two) can win, so while the game has the typical reality show eliminations, these wilderness enthusiasts must work together in order to take the money. In the same way that The Traitors creates a tension between competition and cooperation via its communal prize pot, Outlast sees its contestants forced to maintain relationships whether they like it or not. Stream Outlast on Netflix.

Sources indicate that the tasks on Traitors aren't typically the most thrilling part of the show, which makes this James Bond-branded competition a solid match if you want more complicated and better developed challenges. In this one, nine teams of two visit exotic locations in each episode and compete in spy-themed activities with the ultimate goal of winning £1 million by making it to the end. It leaves out the bits where people sit around a castle strategizing, but it includes, like Traitors, a dapper Scotsman not afraid to camp it up—in this case, Brian Cox, serving as the spymaster who directs the teams in their missions. Stream 007: Road to a Million on Prime Video.

Squid Game: The Challenge would probably be a more reasonable choice for this list—given that it's a proper reality show and not a blood-chilling thriller. But I'm sticking with the original drama here since, as perfectly entertaining as that spin-off is, it feels like it misses the point. In the original (surprise smash hit) drama, 454 needy contestants are recruited for a latest reality competition in which they're tasked to play rather simple children's games—with deadly consequences that are cheered on by the wealthy financiers who are willing to pay good money to watch both the poors go at each other, as people turn on each other to survive and to win the rather shockingly large prize. A bit like The Traitors if all of Alan's murder schtick were literally true. Stream Squid Game on Netflix.

According to recent reports, unity's next venture, amidst rumours of it being bought out by the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund, is the Unity Fellowship, a grant program that offers $50k in cash to Unity-using indie devs that initiative release a game within a year - without asking for recoup, revenue share, creative control or IP ownership in exchange. I don't need to tell you that all sounds too good to be true, even with the Unity engine requirement, but in fairness, the manufacturer has form for handing out cash. The Unity for Humanity grant, just earlier this year, spread $600K across ten different indie projects focused on societal and environmental issues.

It has been revealed that unity states that ten recipient studios will receive the Fellowship's cash grant, as well as direct partnership with Unity staff, industry connections, spots at Unity events and PR/marketing support. Even studios with an existing publisher can apply, if they think that "the Fellowship could still make a real difference for your game." It also clarifies that their policy regarding AI use is that "We don't require you to list the tools you used, but you must own or hold the rights to everything in your game, including any AI-generated content", which doesn't come as a huge surprise considering Unity's excitement around its Unity Spark game-generating AI tool.

The grant is also not open to "countries or regions subject to U.S. sanctions", such as Russia, Iran and Cuba, as well as Brazil, Italy and Quebec due to "local regulations." For developers not in those areas, applications for the grant are open until December 18th, with the recipients to be notified by the end of February 2027. If you're a developer who's interested, you can apply here.

Firaxis reportedly cuts a third of its staff as studio head departs and new XCOM struggles

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Civilization and XCOM developer Firaxis Games has laid off around 60 people.
  • It has been revealed that the cuts, which took place today, account for about a third of the studio’s staff, Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar with the matter.
  • Its sources say Firaxis' unannounced XCOM game has faced development struggles and missed "a significant milestone over the summer".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Civilization and XCOM developer Firaxis Games has laid off around 60 people.

It has been revealed that the cuts, which took place today, account for about a third of the studio’s staff, Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar with the matter. Studio head Heather Hazen is also leaving.

Its sources say Firaxis' unannounced XCOM game has faced development struggles and missed "a significant milestone over the summer". The project will continue, but "may face a shakeup as a result of the cuts".

A spokesperson for 2K, the Take-Two label that runs Firaxis, confirmed Hazen's departure to Bloomberg, and said the studio is "restructuring and recentering around the studio's core strength - designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years".

According to recent reports, "As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis," the spokesperson continued. "These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis.".

The layoffs come two days before the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, which is developed and published by Rockstar, a separate label at Take-Two.

In September, around 18 months after Civ 7's widely criticised launch - and as the legendary 4X series celebrates its 35th anniversary - Firaxis unveiled a host of new updates coming to the game as it continued to improve it. These included an atomic age enhancement, dragging Civ 7 into the present and beyond, as well as its first paid expansion, Earthrise, both arriving next year.

Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick admitted earlier this year that the studio "got it wrong with Civ 7".

Recent findings suggest that "The game is a really good game. And it's certainly a profitable enterprise for us. But this is one where I think what we tried to do was a bridge too far, from the consumer's perspective," he told Game File in May.

It’s not the first round of cuts at the studio - 2K confirmed an unspecified number of layoffs at Firaxis in September 2025, and around 30 jobs went in 2023.

Latest Update: Robert Downey Jr., Chris Evans, the Russo brothers, and more on the making of Avengers: Infinity War

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The countdown to Avengers: Doomsday is almost over.
  • Pulled from the May 2018 issue of Total Film magazine, this time capsule feature is a fascinating snapshot of the MCU ahead of its biggest (and arguably best) movie, with candid insight from Robert Downey Jr., Chris Evans, Chadwick Boseman, Tom Holland, Elizabeth Olsen, the Russo brothers and many, many more.
  • Avengers: Doomsday is one of this year's (and any year's) most exciting upcoming movies, and there's no better time to revisit a crucial chapter on the road to Doomsday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The countdown to Avengers: Doomsday is almost over. Years after Robert Downey Jr.'s return as Doctor Doom was revealed on stage at San Diego Comic-Con, we're on the precipice of Doom's MCU debut, and to celebrate, we're taking a Stark Tech time machine back to 2018, when Total Film reported from the set of Avengers: Infinity War.

Pulled from the May 2018 issue of Total Film magazine, this time capsule feature is a fascinating snapshot of the MCU ahead of its biggest (and arguably best) movie, with candid insight from Robert Downey Jr., Chris Evans, Chadwick Boseman, Tom Holland, Elizabeth Olsen, the Russo brothers and many, many more.

Avengers: Doomsday is one of this year's (and any year's) most exciting upcoming movies, and there's no better time to revisit a crucial chapter on the road to Doomsday. When you're done reading this time capsule set report, be sure to check out our own experience revisiting the movie, as we consider why Avengers: Infinity War is "essential viewing" ahead of Avengers: Doomsday. But for now, let's take a trip to the set of Avengers: Infinity War….

It has been revealed that pinewood Atlanta Studios, 2017. Total Film is on the top-secret set of Avengers: Infinity War, one of the few remaining instalments in the Marvel Cinematic Universe's Phase Three, and the culmination of the 18 previous MCU movies to date. It's the most ambitious team-up yet for a studio that pioneered the concept of assembling disparate heroes onscreen in an 'expanded universe'.

Industry observers note that at Chris 'Star-Lord' Pratt's estimate, there are 22 superheroes uniting to face down the ultimate big bad. What TF witnesses on Stage 9 is just a hint of the carnage that intergalactic villain Thanos (played by Josh Brolin, via motion-capture) will wreak when he comes to Earth to enact his grand blueprint. Fire. Twisted metal. Fallen trees. Soil and gravel everywhere.

According to recent reports, crew members ensure that the fires are burning just where they need to be, as dozens of cast and stunt performers prepare to run purposefully out of a trench for a slow-motion shot. Details are scarce as to what's actually going on, but it's fair to assume something major has occurred. Avengers rub shoulders with Guardians, as Wakandan warriors take up arms alongside characters who look like they've stepped through a portal from another realm entirely.

Mark Ruffalo – in strategically spotted skin-tight pyjamas – has a mast attached to his head to indicate the Hulk's eyeline and the scale of his CGI avatar. By any measure – creative, logistical, and presumably budgetary – this is the biggest Marvel movie yet. Hydraulic canisters hiss, and bangs break out when action's called and the cameras roll.

When we later catch up with the cast, snatching chats with handfuls of Avengers at a time, their bloodied and bruised faces attest to the trouble the superteam has found themselves in. But for now, the sheer scale of this diorama of destruction is jaw-dropping. "It's truly like herding cats," Captain America actor Chris Evans jokes to TF of the enormo-cast. "I look at the first AD, this poor guy. It's just hard to get everybody focused.".

During a break in filming, writers Christopher Markus and Stephen McFeely (of all three Captain America movies) explain how they solved the challenge of incorporating so many heroes into one film: making genocidal Titan warlord Thanos the main character. Having been teased since the mid-credits sting of 2012's The Avengers, Thanos is finally taking his place in the sun.

"The thing that separates it from other Avengers movies for me is that the antagonist is the main character," says McFeely. "So in many ways, this is Thanos's movie. It was the smartest way for us to accommodate all the characters and honour this [villain] that Marvel's been teasing for so long.".

When asked how high the stakes are, McFeely offers, "Is the universe high enough for you?" The Mad Titan has some high-minded ideals about how the universe should be, and his blueprint involves wiping out about half of its inhabitants. In order to set his plan in motion, he needs six MacGuffins that have been seeded throughout the series so far: the Infinity Stones, which will slot into his golden gauntlet and give him godlike powers.

Sources indicate that "He wants six Infinity Stones," explains Markus. "And once you get them, you can do whatever you want." It goes some way towards explaining why quite such an exhaustive roster of heroes is required to even begin to fight off such an omnipotent foe and his "elite squad," the Black Order. But, following the events of Civil War, the divided superteam are at a low ebb.

Recent findings suggest that "I mean, the whole point of doing Civil War was that they enter this movie fractured and separated, and that will play a very integral part of the film," explains Joe Russo, one half of the director duo, the Russo brothers. In Infinity War, the core Avengers – Iron Man, Cap, Thor, Black Widow, Hulk, et al. – will be joined by Black Panther, Spider-Man, Doctor Strange, the Guardians Of The frickin' Galaxy, and more.

So, after the head-to-head in Civil War, has the relationship between Iron Man and Cap improved at all? "I don't know that it could have gotten any worse," considers Evans when we catch him between takes, clad in his Cap suit, sans helmet and chest-piece, his face dirtied from the day's action. Robert Downey Jr. – the Iron Man star who was integral to kicking off the entire MCU – concurs.

Recent findings suggest that "I wouldn't say he does [get on with Cap]," Downey Jr. explains, holding court with the laid-back confidence of a talk show host. "I'm saying that because Thanos is the threat. I don't think it can be underestimated. It's not just what Josh Brolin is bringing to his portrayal of it, but there's something about it where we've all agreed that this is the sum of all of our fears. It's like Gestalt therapy at this point.".

Sources indicate that currently dressed in a camo T-shirt and hoodie, the (fake) blood above RDJ's eyebrow attests to a pretty physical form of therapy. "I think because the threat has risen to a latest level – which is really saying something – that whether we want to band together or not, we won't survive unless we do," he continues. "So I think that's a bit of a new thing. So it's like, 'Can these disparate heroes get along after all?'".

Chris Hemsworth – out of his Thor costume and wearing a dressing gown over a black T-shirt and jogging bottoms – attests to the scale of the threat. "I think that [Thanos is] the strongest thing we've ever faced, his force," he states in his Aussie baritone. "And it brings out a whole other level of us, I think, and another stage or journey we need to embark on.".

Sources indicate that tom Holland strolls over to join Downey Jr. and Hemsworth. Munching on a banana to keep up his calorie intake, he's clad in black mo-cap pyjamas (a requirement of his upgraded Spider-Man suit), with a puffer jacket to keep him warm in the empty neighbouring soundstage we're now occupying, and he's sporting a bloodied nose.

Recent findings suggest that keen to avoid dropping spoilers (as he's been known to do on social media), Holland's staying tight-lipped about Peter Parker's journey, although he does tease that "he matures a lot", before Downey Jr. adds with a sly grin: "Things you wouldn't expect are endured.".

Dishing out the cuts and bruises is Thanos, who'll draw all the other characters into his orbit. Having a bad guy at the forefront will mark a real change of pace for the typically hero-heavy MCU, and means that Thanos needs the requisite depth to carry the film.

Industry observers note that "We were considering showing his backstory," notes Anthony Russo, "but ultimately felt it wasn't necessary for the movie. However, the movie is told from his point of view. I think it's a very interesting space for an audience to be in, because every villain thinks they're the hero of their own story. We thought it'd become compelling to track a villain's point of view through a movie.".

Anthony Russo goes on to call Brolin's performance "stunning", explaining that he brings "an intensity and a violence, but also at the same time, a charm and a sensitivity. It's a very complicated character. He's at times despicable and horrifying, and at other times oddly empathetic.".

Because the threat has risen to a new level, whether we want to band together or not, we won't survive unless we do.

Industry observers note that having Brolin on set (albeit in those unavoidable mo-cap pyjamas) gives the digital character added heft, as well as providing the actors with something to work against. "It really is mind-blowing how sensitive a performance we can translate into a CG character now, and how much of Josh's performance is in that character," adds Joe Russo.

"He brings some humanity to something that could just be a one-dimensional villain," says Karen Gillan, her friendly Scottish accent bizarrely contrasting with the menacing blue makeup she's covered in to play Gamora. "I can't look him in the eye, but I hear his voice," says Black Panther star Chadwick Boseman of working opposite Brolin when he's mo-capping an eight-foot-tall character. "He's right there.".

Yes, Black Panther and his Wakandan allies will play a crucial part in Infinity War, with the third-act battle set to go down on his home turf. Given the astonishing success of T'Challa's recent solo movie, his presence will only heighten the anticipation for Infinity War. "Being able to bring that energy into Infinity War, and that dimensionality and those themes into our movie, it's a gift for us," beams Joe Russo.

When we speak to Boseman on set, he looks like one cool cat in his full Panther get-up (minus the mask), even with a long coat draped over his shoulders.

"How does he fit in as an Avenger?" Boseman considers. "I don't know if it's a situation where it's like a club that you join. I think the fact that Wakanda, to a certain degree, opens up a fresh place for the Avengers to fit. As opposed to him fitting into the Avengers, he opens up a new space. And that's pretty much all I can say." That charismatic chuckle booms. "That's all I can say!".

In a recent development, boseman is just one of several newly successful solo characters who'll be joining the Avengers lineup. "It's like Voltron, you know what I mean?" quips Evans of the characters uniting. "This other franchise starts doing well, and they start forming one giant thing. It's really exciting.".

Avengers: Infinity War 5* review: "Bold, ballsy, satisfying, and dramatic".

It has been revealed that benedict Cumberbatch's Doctor Strange will also play a key role, being brought into the fold with Wong (Benedict Wong) via Tony Stark and Bruce Banner/Hulk (Ruffalo). Holland's Spidey also returns after high-school spin Homecoming. "I would have been first in line to see The Avengers, so to be on an Avengers film set as a 21-year-old is surreal," Holland enthuses, grinning like, well, a 21-year-old on an Avengers film set.

Hemsworth, mock-disgruntled, chips in: "What makes me laugh about this whole thing is, it was not too long ago that [I was being asked]: 'What's it like to be the newly introduced one?' I'm like, 'Oh my God, I'm getting really old.' I'm the past now. This is the future. It's the transition." Hot on the heels of Thor: Ragnarok, the gut-bustingly funny threequel that saw Thor and Hulk flexing their comedic muscles, that duo will find themselves in a slightly more serious predicament this time out.

"God knows I tried [to be funny]," laughs Ruffalo, his face still dotted with mo-cap markers. "It's the Russo brothers, so it's not quite as comedic. Of course, we're fighting Thanos, and that's not funny. But we tried to keep some of that spontaneous combustion alive. Banner's very, very different in this movie. They're all really different. I feel like I've been lucky. I got to do this character in steps, and I have had a plotted-out arc of how this character's developed and changed over all these movies. So you're going to see another surprising incarnation of Banner.".

Also returning, and last seen in Civil War, is Elizabeth Olsen's Scarlet Witch. Her fledgling relationship with Vision (Paul Bettany) was hinted at in that film, and will be explored further here. "It was a lot of fun for Paul and me," says Olsen, her character's fingerless gloves peeking out from the sleeves of her black coat. "I think we didn't know if we were going to, I guess, scratch that itch of those characters and their relationship. So we've kind of layered it in since [Avengers: Age Of] Ultron. Now we actually got to fulfil that throughline, which was actually really cool, to have something to really anchor us to the film.".

Recent findings suggest that although the fact that Vision's forehead bears one of the Infinity Stones that Thanos wants might impact their courtship. As well as putting existing relationships under stress, having this many heroes on screen throws up opportunities for unexpected character-combos. "That's one of the fun things that's going to happen in these two movies, those introductions of those characters to each other," notes Don 'War Machine' Cheadle, sporting the unofficial uniform of, yep, mo-cap PJs. "Everyone's kind of like, 'Who is this dude? I don't know why you guys are even here!' We get to throw them all together and see how they respond to each other.".

Of course, franchise stalwart Black Widow (Scarlett Johansson) returns, as does former Winter Soldier Bucky Barnes (Sebastian Stan), Falcon (Anthony Mackie) and Hawkeye (Jeremy Renner), who has been seen sporting a newly introduced mohawk but has been absent from all trailers so far. "All will be explained when people see the movie," teases Anthony Russo of Hawkeye's absence. "It's all tied into the story.".

In a recent development, although the one group of characters who could really shake things up are the Guardians Of The Galaxy, the ragtag team of spacefarers who have little regard for traditional heroics, and strut to their own mixtape beat. From the first trailer, when Thor spies the bunch of a-holes and asks, "Who the hell are you guys?", the chemistry seemed inevitable.

That moment is Downey Jr.'s favourite of the whole film: "I'm like, 'Sold!' If the whole third movie was that scene, we're fine, because the Guardians are also just a whole other wackadoo, awesome, super-creative integer." When we talk to Star-Lord himself, Chris Pratt, he's wearing his signature red leather jacket and also has a dirtied, bloody face.

Recent findings suggest that "The stakes have never been higher," he claims between forkfuls of lunch from a Tupperware pot (the cast and crew are working 'French hours' and eating on the fly). "All the movies have led towards this. You couldn't just have any old standard villain. You have to have the one villain who touched every one of those characters' storylines.".

In a recent development, "Well, I sensed glory, but I will tell you this: I just have such pride. Really, honestly, the main thing is, I think we really have become this oddball family that genuinely looks after and cares for each other, and supports each other. So that's a first for me. The other thing is, none of us would be here at this stage without Joss [Whedon]. Because he did a proof-of-concept execution that was monumental. But then there's been a quantum – literally – shift in the way that things are going now, where all these different franchises are on the horizon, and they're bringing upcoming energy, and some of us are maybe tapping out or going away. Who knows what the future is? But the task is yet to be completed. I don't think I've been hoisted up in a chair and marched around yet like I deserve, but we'll see.".

It has been revealed that asked if he's changed his approach to playing Peter Quill after jumping from the relatively MCU-isolated Guardians movies to this multi-character sandbox, Pratt responds, "I guess a little bit. We get to bring some of the Guardians' flavor to this movie, which is nice. You get to be a little more vibrant, a little more irreverent, a little more colourful. So you're not carrying the dramatic weight or anything like that.".

On how the Avengers experience compares to Guardians, Pom 'Mantis' Klementieff gasps, "It's massive..." GOTG Vol.2's scene-pinching empath currently has two small antennae sprouting from her head that'll be boosted in post-production. "There are so many people, and so many incredible actors. The Guardians set felt more like a family because we all know each other. But [here] we start knowing more about the others, and then we're going to wrap...".

Speaking of family, there's another reason the Guardians will be significant for Infinity War: both Nebula and Gamora (Zoe Saldana) were raised as Thanos' 'daughters', before breaking away. "What can I say?" grins Karen Gillan. "This is where I get nervous because I'm going to give away spoilers. It's definitely going to be explored further. Her relationship with Gamora is going to get really interesting because of a certain element that I can't tell you...".

"I don't even know what you're talking about," cuts in Olsen (most actors didn't get a complete script). "Oh, it's so good," laughs Gillan in response. "It's so good. It's going to be great." Chris Evans was one of the few to get a complete script. "I luckily was able to get a script," smiles Evans. "The majority of people on set are like, 'So what are we doing today?' The Russos have to give a loose description of what's happening. I didn't complain. I was just like, 'Give me a fucking script! Give me a script. I need to know what's going on!'".

Recent findings suggest that what could make Infinity War (and Avengers: Endgame ) so monumental is that it arrives at the time when the MCU is welcoming a lot of fresh blood, while older contracts might be coming to an end. This could be a time of metamorphosis and reinvigoration. Naturally, cast and crew avoid spoilers, but they do promise that the roster is in for a shake-up, and we could see some permanent exits.

According to recent reports, "We have not had any special death requests," states McFeely, but co-writer Markus says that Marvel was open to anything, and they had free rein to kill off whomever the story dictated should go. "You don't want to… I'm talking around things," stutters Markus. "You don't want to cut off a flower just as it's beginning to bloom… But a nice big flower maybe you could.".

Sources indicate that "It's one of the reasons these movies can be special, because Kevin [Feige, Marvel Studios president] and the rest of Marvel allow us big swings, right?" adds McFeely. "There wasn't a mandate that everything has to get tied up so that we can continue with another one. I feel these movies are most successful when the characters undergo big changes, and – in our case – when someone is escorted off the stage. So that allows for some really good storytelling.".

"It's a cocktail of emotions," says Evans of this beginning of the end of a particular era of the MCU. "It's nice because it really has evolved the way you would hope." For all the talk of death, the atmosphere on set isn't morose, and the camaraderie of the cast is evident. After all, they've had enough films to forge a bond on, and they're clearly enjoying being part of such an expansive repertory.

I didn't complain. I was just like, 'Give me a fucking script! Give me a script. I need to know what's going on!'.

"I've never felt like a fan as much as I have on these films," grins Hemsworth. "Like meeting [the Guardians] as Thor, but also as Chris, was equally as exciting and fresh, and it brought in a whole different energy. Especially these last few days, we've had just about every member of the Marvel Universe on the set.".

In a recent development, "It's been the Ben-Hur of the MCU, for sure," chimes Downey Jr. Now, the gang are looking ahead to Avengers: Endgame, which arrives in 2019, and was shot back-to-back with Infinity War. When we catch up with the Russos again in March 2018, they've "locked" picture on Infinity War and are in the final stages of tweaking VFX and sound, and they once again assure that Infinity War and Endgame will be two very separate films (rather than being 'half' a movie each).

"We're very, very happy with it, and we're very excited with where the story goes," says Joe Russo. "I think it's going to be really surprising to audiences. We're excited for the anticipation that that will create for Avengers: Endgame. They're very distinctly different movies. I think that people will be pleased with the fact that they get different styles and tones in both films, and different narratives."'.

The cast and filmmakers couldn't be more excited about how fans are going to react to the two upcoming movies (which will have Ant-Man and the Wasp and Captain Marvel sandwiched between them). "It's going to be messy," Ruffalo claims of the audience reaction. "There's going to be a lot of messes in the theater. Heads exploded… People pooping their pants.".

It has been revealed that "I wasn't going to say that, but you're right," laughs Boseman. "This one, it does have that sense of a finale," adds Pratt. "Have you ever seen a great fireworks show, and you're like, 'How the fuck did they do that?' It gives you goosebumps. That's this movie. That's this combination of movies.".

"Yeah," admits Pratt, "It's true.".

Five Things I Wish I'd Known Before Getting a Foldable Phone

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The iPhone Duo might be the highest profile foldable phone to date, but it’s by no means the first.
  • Sources indicate that one of the most notable aspects of the iPhone Duo is how wide its screen is, even while closed.
  • It has been revealed that compare with my Pixel 11 Pro Fold, which features an extremely tall 2.17:1 aspect ratio when closed, but a nearly square 1:04:1 aspect ratio when open.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The iPhone Duo might be the highest profile foldable phone to date, but it’s by no means the first. Personally, I’ve had my eye on the Google variant, the Pixel 11 Pro Fold—and recently I finally took the plunge. I thought I’d done my research to know how different having a foldable phone would be, but I still had a bit to learn. Here are some of the things I wish I’ve learned along the way after making the jump to foldables.

Sources indicate that one of the most notable aspects of the iPhone Duo is how wide its screen is, even while closed. And there’s a good reason for that: The larger screen while open has exactly the same 1.41:1 aspect ratio as the smaller screen while closed. This has a ripple effect on how every app you use looks and feels—and whether you like Apple’s approach is largely a matter of personal preference.

It has been revealed that compare with my Pixel 11 Pro Fold, which features an extremely tall 2.17:1 aspect ratio when closed, but a nearly square 1:04:1 aspect ratio when open. On the outer screen, apps are a little less wide than on my old phone, but there’s plenty of space for reading books or articles on the inner screen.

According to recent reports, I like the tall, thin display personally because it feels easier to reach buttons with my thumb, and the wider display is better for reading. However, this approach can occasionally result in some odd app layouts. Not every app is designed for tablets, especially on Android, and shifting the aspect ratio between the inner and outer display sometimes means re-rendering or even restarting an app entirely to load properly.

It has been revealed that the iPhone Duo has a more consistent aspect ratio and general feel between the inner and outer display, but it comes at the cost of a really wide phone. Neither approach is better or worse on its own, but it might be worth going to a local store to get your hands on the phone you’re thinking about before buying.

Industry observers note that for years, the screens on most smartphones have been made of increasingly tough and scratch-resistant glass. So tough that you might not even need a screen protector anymore. On a foldable phone, that can be true of the outside display, but it’s very much not when it comes to the inner, foldable display.

Screens might be foldable, but the strong, durable glass that makes your phone so scratch-resistant isn’t. No matter what foldable phone you use, the covering on the inner display will be more flexible, and thus softer. Apple uses a nano-texture polymer film that can be replaced, but the film on most foldable phones cannot. That means if they get damaged or scratched, those marks will be there for the life of your phone.

If you (like me) haven’t considered a screen protector in a while, it might be time to try one again, at least for the inner display. It’s also worth keeping in mind how rough you strategy to be with your phone. Construction sites or factories might not be the best home for a foldable phone you plan to open a lot, but an office job should be a bit safer.

Industry observers note that similar to the screen protector matter, cases can be more of a headache. Most rigid cases will come in two pieces, and the piece that covers the outer display can be shockingly minimal—barely more than a frame, for some of the cases I looked at. A poorly made case can be brittle or pop off more easily, so it’s more notable to get a high-quality one.

According to recent reports, if you like to use your phone case as your wallet, it’s also notable to be wary of cases that aren’t specifically designed for your model of phone (and maybe some that are). A lot of wallet cases are built to unfold to reveal your phone’s screen on one side, and your cards and ID on the other. But depending on how your foldable phone unfolds, it could be awkward to reach the inner screen.

The hinge also introduces more spaces for dust and debris to get into your phone. Despite the extra moving parts and gaps, most foldable phones still offer the now-standard IP68 dust and water resistance rating. That mainly applies to what can get inside and damage the components inside your phone. It’s still possible for hair and dirt to get gummed up in any pinchable spaces, so look out for any case that might provide even more nooks for dust to collect in.

I’ve set up most of my apps how I like them by now, but when I first got my foldable phone, I had to revisit some settings I thought I was done messing with. One of the most notable examples was my ebook apps: I was previously using a single-column, medium-font layout, but it looked ridiculous on the inner display. After switching to a two-column layout, it not only felt more natural, but a lot like reading a regular book.

Similarly, there were some uses for my calendar app that got a whole lot more useful. I’ve never really been able to use anything other than either the one-day or Schedule view if I want to make out anything, but on the inner screen, I can finally look at my week at a glance. But that meant tweaking some things—like showing reminders, which fit naturally amid my events in Schedule view, but become a cluttered mess when I saw 14 different reminders to take my meds at once in the Week view.

Most apps do a decent job of automatically adjusting to different screen sizes, but I found a few outliers that I had to figure out myself. As an example, Google Docs would default to a view with extremely tiny text when I first started using it. It took me a bit to figure out that this was due to a “Print layout” toggle in the document’s settings. This is, for some reason, enabled by default when opening a document on the larger inner screen. It can take some time to learn the eccentricities of all your apps, but it’s worth poking around when you can.

I know, it sounds so obvious, right? The outer screen is the one you’ll use most often, so how could you forget about it? But when you unfold the inner screen, the outer one is still useful in some surprising ways that I hadn’t even considered until I went poking around in some of my apps.

Industry observers note that one of the most adorable examples is the Made You Look feature in the Pixel’s Camera app. When unfolded, you can take a picture using the rear camera and see a preview like normal, while the outer screen shows silly animations to capture the attention of a baby or toddler that you want to look into the camera. Admittedly, this is an older feature, but it’s a clever one. For adults, you can also use the outer display to get a selfie preview while using the rear-facing camera.

The outer screen is also just better for some things. YouTube is one of the few apps that has a unique layout designed for a partially folded screen, with the video playing on the tilted-up portion of the screen, and video controls on the bottom portion.

Recent findings suggest that however, in my experience, it was a lot nicer to watch a YouTube video by just propping up the outer screen by unfolding the phone a bit, like a kickstand. My Pixel even detected when YouTube was in full-screen mode on the outer display and would be more forgiving of unfolding the phone without switching to the inner screen. The phone anticipated I might just want to prop up the smaller screen, which I thought was a nice touch.
